recipes.name: Wedge Salad with Blue Cheese Dressing
ingredients_raw: 1 head iceberg lettuce, cut into 8 wedges

steps.text: Combine 1/2 of the blue cheese, mayonnaise, buttermilk, vinegar, sour cream, sugar, olive oil, garlic, and pepper in a bowl; blend with an electric hand mixer until well combined. Cover and chill in the refrigerator until serving.
Place each lettuce wedge on a salad plate. Drizzle dressing over each wedge. Scatter tomatoes, onion, and remaining blue cheese over each salad.

raw_recipe.headline: Wedge Salad with Blue Cheese Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This wedge salad recipe features crisp iceberg lettuce topped with a chilled and creamy homemade blue cheese dressing for a classic, elegant appetizer.

video.description: This elegant salad is all about the dressing, and this one really packs in the flavor! Combine blue cheese with sour cream, buttermilk, mayonnaise, red wine vinegar, olive oil, sugar, minced garlic and black pepper and give a good chill. Then place wedges of iceberg lettuce on plates, drizzle on the dressing and scatter on diced tomatoes, thin slices of red onion and blue cheese crumbles. To make extra special, add some bacon crumbles, too. Delicious for lunches or for impressing at an elegant dinner party.

review.reviewBody:
I love this dressing. But like the other reviewer, that is alot of blue cheese. I just added about 1/4 cup(eyeballed it), put it all in a blender for a few pulses, and I have to say, it is the best I've tasted. Even my kids love it, and ask for it all the time. Now I keep blue cheese in stock. It is just ever so slightly sweet when you first taste it, then you get the nice tang following that, with the nice strong flavor of the cheese. I have never cared for bottled dressing of any kind, I have always liked making my own because I like to be able to control the salt and sugar and it just is always nice and fresh.
I wonder if the recipe might have been a typo or something. Maybe it meant to be a half a cup instead. This is the only reason as to why I had to give it a 4 star. I also like adding to it chopped candied walnuts, chopped bacon, and chopped granny smith apples. It just doesn't get any better.

Years ago I made a similar salad. I placed a wedge on each of 2 plates and they looked great. I was so proud of my efforts. My husband began to eat and very soon found an angleworm lodged between the leaves. My suggestion is that the lettuce head should be soaked in salt water for some time in order to remove unwanted seasonings.

This was sooooo good. And easy to make. I mixed the dressing with a fork and that left nice big lumps of the blue cheese so I didn't have to use so many sprinkles of it later. I also chopped up a handfull of pecans to add a nice crunch. The dressing is better the second day so you might want to make it the day before.
YUM! The only difference I made instead was the "homemade" dressing, I used homemade Uncle Dan's dressing. I also added some crumbled bacon. Definately will be serving this one again.

Delicious. Pretty sure the dressing recipe means 1/2 a cup of blue cheese though instead of 1/2 a pound. I used 1/4 cup and it was great. The recipe made about two cups of dressing too, so those cooking for a smaller group may want to cut it in half. Applewood smoked bacon is a must on top of this salad though!

Really liked it! Surprisingly easy and very refreshing. I didn't have any buttermilk, but I added vinegar and milk...it did the trick. I didn't chill overnight, but my cold ingredients did more than fine!

This a replica of "Shula's" bleu cheese dressing and is out of this world! I add extra garlic and bleu cheese. I use an immersion blender so this comes together very quickly! Red onions are a must. I could drink this, it's that yummy;-)

This recipe is SO close to the dressing served at Morton's in Chicago! It is to DIE FOR!! I made as recipe calls the first time. It was absolutely delicious. The second time, I was looking to lighten the calorie content and used light mayo, light sour cream, and Splenda. Taste really did not change - just slight texture. I will make with fewer calories from now on. This salad is now a part of our regular rotation!! Thank you for this terrific recipe!! And according to My Fitness Pal (I entered all ingredients and they spit out a total calories per serving), each serving has been reduced from 362 calories per serving to 140 calories per serving!!

This is a great recipe. I have made this dressing many times now with some variations. For my taste, I kept the 1/2 cup of blue cheese, used more garlic (2 tsp) and no sugar. It definitely tastes better the longer it's kept refrigerated to allow the flavors to blend.

This salad was a hit with my guests who are Wedge Salad aficionados. Followed the recipe with minor changes based on very helpful comments from reviewers. Used only 1/2 cup of crumbled blue cheese; only 1 Tbsp of vinegar (I'm not a big fan of vinegar); substituted 1/4 tsp of garlic powder for the garlic glove; used red onion but certainly not a whole one; added 1/2 lb. bacon and topped with scattered craisins. Rated 4 stars only because of some portion inconsistencies. Will certainly make again.

This is a great recipe. I cut both sugar and blue cheese by about a third. Will cut sugar more and probably try to use the same amount of better quality blue cheese next time. This is a real keeper and would be great as a creamy garlic without the blue cheese.
I have served this recipe many times, although I prefer to use less sugar.

We loved this! I,too, used WAY less bleu cheese. (I see other comments on this recipe about using aPOUND of BC) I used one container of store bought bleu cheese crumbles. There was enough for the recipe and enough to sprinkle over the finished salads. I found it a bit sweet so next time I will add less sugar. I also added crisp home fried bacon crumbled over the top of the wedges before serving. This turned out so nice we will definitely do this again. The nice thing is the dressing is versatile enough to put on steaks as well.

Love the dressing. We have this as a meal, so added bacon. Also, there is a steakhouse in a casino near us that plates the lettuce on Catalina dressing, then adds the rest of ingredients, and tops with blue cheese dressing. It is decadent! The only way I serve it now
Absolutely delicious! Thank you for sharing this.
This blue cheese dressing is absolutely delicious. Definitely a keeper. Will never buy blue cheese dressing again!
This is our favorite dressing. I added a small amount of sugar.

I notice that everyone who gave this 4 or 5 stars, and as shown in most of the photos, added bacon. There is no bacon in the recipe. I have never tasted vinegar in store bought or restaurant blue cheese but you sure can taste it in this recipe. Will stick with Litehouse brand.
If you leave out the sugar, vinegar, and oil and use only enough milk to thin it out to desired consistency. You'll have a good dressing. Add the blue cheese at the end for a nice chunky dressing.
Great base recipe - we left out the sugar, buttermilk and tomato. Perfect accompaniment for our surf and turf dinner!
